explanation: A prophet in Babylon and one of the Jewish youths taken captive by Nebuchadnezzar. He is known for his wisdom and faithfulness to God.
A place where lions were kept, into which Daniel was thrown as punishment for praying to God instead of King Darius.
Ruler over the Persian Empire that conquered Babylon. He respected Daniel but was tricked into signing a law that led to Daniel's punishment.
Communication between people and God, which Daniel faithfully practiced three times a day, even when it was forbidden.
Supernatural beings who serve as God's messengers and servants. An angel protected Daniel in the lions' den.
Daniel's unwavering faith in God led Him to protect him from the lions in the lions' den.
A plot by some of Darius' officials who wanted Daniel removed from his position by manipulating the king into issuing a law against prayer.
